transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… mostly it’s my concentration. It’s gotten unreliable. I’ll be looking over a chart at the clinic, or even working on a watercolor, and then I realize I’ve read the same line three times. My mind just sort of runs off to everything that could go wrong.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when you try not to?

Yes… I do. I try to talk myself out of it, sort of reason through it like I would with a nervous patient. But it doesn’t really stop there. One concern just leads to another, and before I know it I’m checking emails again, going back over notes, asking the same questions… instead of just letting it be.
Are your worries mostly about one particular stressor in your life right now, or do they tend to spread across many different parts of life?

It’s not just one thing, no. It sort of moves around… old patients, whether they’re being taken care of properly, the finances of handing off the practice, what I’m supposed to be once I’m fully retired. Even saying it out loud, it feels bigger than it probably should.
For at least the past six months, have you been worrying like this on most days?
Yes. It’s been… more than six months. I’d say it really started when I began the formal retirement process, about a year and a few months ago. Since then it’s been there most days.
Do you often feel physically tense or unable to relax?
I’m not sure. I mean… I suppose I’m not as relaxed as I used to be, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m physically tense.
Do you get tired easily?

Yes… I do. By midafternoon I’m often pretty worn out. It’s not always fixed by taking it easy, either. Even small things like working in the garden or standing at the easel feel heavier than they used to.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know… not exactly depressed, I wouldn’t say. Maybe a bit low some days, but I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
I’m not really sure. Maybe sometimes I feel a bit unsettled, but I wouldn’t say I’ve paid close attention to it.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?
I don’t really remember having a big problem with that as a child. School was… fine, as far as I can recall. Nothing that stands out.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worry?

Yes… I suppose it can be hard to stop. I try to talk myself through it, like I would with a nervous patient, but then one concern turns into another. Before I know it I’m checking emails or going over notes again, or asking the same thing twice, instead of just letting it go.
Have you been more irritable than usual?
I’m not sure. I don’t think so, not noticeably… maybe I get a bit short sometimes, but I haven’t really been tracking it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes… most nights, I’d say. I get into bed tired, but once it’s quiet I start going over things—patient transfers, money details, that sort of thing. Even if I do sleep, I’m often up around four or five and don’t feel like I really settled.
Have you been enjoying your usual activities less than you used to?
I don’t know… not especially, I suppose. I haven’t really noticed a big change there.
On most days lately, have you been feeling down or depressed?
Not really, no. I mean… I wouldn’t say depressed. Maybe worn out at times, but I haven’t been feeling down most days.
Do you feel these worries are mainly tied to your retirement and handing off the practice?

Partly, yes. The retirement and handing off the practice is a lot of it… but it sort of spreads. I keep thinking about whether my patients are being looked after properly, whether the money side of the handoff is solid, and… I suppose whether I’ll be of any use once I’m fully out of it. It feels like more worry than the situation really calls for, if I’m honest.
Do you feel your worrying is more than would be expected for the retirement situation?

Yes… I think so. Even to me it feels a bit out of proportion. My mind just keeps going around it — the patients, the money side of the handoff, what I’m supposed to be once I’m not working. It’s more than it probably needs to be.
Do you often have trouble relaxing?

Yes… I do. I try to talk myself through it, the way I would with a nervous patient, but it doesn’t really settle. One concern leads to another, and before I know it I’m checking emails or going over notes again instead of just letting it be.
Is this anxiety interfering with your day-to-day functioning?

Yes… somewhat. I’ve had to slow down the handoff more than I meant to. I keep second-guessing things and losing time at the clinic.

Even things outside work — painting, gardening — they don’t feel as easy to manage lately.
